description:
We are a passionate team interested in AI, Data Science, technology, and space exploration. We love learning, sharing ideas, and solving real-world problems. We welcome creative and motivated members with skills in programming, AI/ML, data analysis, web development, and design.

Our Motto: Think Beyond Earth. Create Beyond Limits!
summary:
Earth Signal is an interactive dashboard that helps anyone see what is changing on Earth, where, by how much, and whether the change is real. We developed a Python analysis engine and a web dashboard for gridded Earth observation data. For each map cell it calculates a trend per decade, tests whether that trend is statistically significant, and grades its reliability. It also finds neighbouring regions that change in opposite directions, which a regional average would hide. Users explore the results through maps, charts, a plain-English report and a checklist of recommended next steps.

It addresses the “Earth System Trend Detective” challenge directly. It turns annual NASA-style data (vegetation, precipitation, soil moisture, temperature and water storage) into clear answers about where trends occur and how strong they are. Our pipeline is designed for NASA open datasets such as MODIS, GPM IMERG, MERRA-2 and GRACE. This prototype is demonstrated on a demo dataset.

It matters because noise in short records can look like a trend. By separating real change from chance, Earth Signal helps scientists, farmers, water managers and planners focus on the places that truly need attention.
details:
What it does and how it works
Earth Signal is an interactive trend detective for gridded Earth observation data. The user picks a variable (vegetation greenness, precipitation, soil moisture, land surface temperature, air temperature or water storage), a region and a confidence level. For every map cell, our Python engine calculates the trend per decade using the Theil-Sen method and tests it with the Mann-Kendall test, corrected for serial correlation. False-discovery control across all cells keeps chance patterns out. Each significant cell receives a Low, Medium or High reliability grade. The tool also finds neighbouring areas that change in opposite directions, which a regional average would hide, and a year-shuffle test checks whether those patterns could be chance.

Users explore the results in a dashboard with insight charts, a clickable trend map, a side-by-side view of all variables, a cell inspector with the trend line, a variable ranking, a plain-English report and a checklist of recommended next steps. Results can be downloaded as a CSV.

Benefits and intended impact
Short records are noisy, and noise can look like a trend. Earth Signal separates real change from chance and shows how much to trust each result. This helps scientists, farmers, water managers and city planners focus on the places that need attention first. The plain-English report makes the findings usable by people without a statistics background.

Tools and technologies
Python (NumPy, xarray, SciPy-style statistics), a standalone HTML and JavaScript dashboard, data pipeline scripts for NASA datasets (MODIS, GPM IMERG, MERRA-2, GRACE), 36 automated tests, and GitHub Pages for hosting.

Creativity
Most trend tools stop at a map of slopes. Earth Signal adds reliability grades, opposite-trend detection, and a written report with recommendations, all in one dashboard that opens with a double-click.

Factors we considered
Statistical honesty (short records, serial correlation, thousands of cells tested at once), clarity for non-technical users, and the fact that trends show association, not cause. Irrigation, land-cover change and sensor changes can all produce trends, so the recommendations include cause-aware checks. The prototype is demonstrated on a demo dataset, and the pipeline is built to run on real NASA files.
